experiment: gameid-crossval — cross-arch BSim + anchored BinDiff for game-TU location
verdict: NEGATIVE — neither signal calibrates well enough to bracket TU spans

bindiff_fresh.note: precision rises with confidence but recall is ~2%; correctly-labeled fns are sparse and non-contiguous

bsim_crossarch.tool: Ghidra 12.2 BSim medium_nosize, RB3Xenon sigs queried vs rb3wii.bsim H2 DB
bsim_crossarch.degenerate_match: 6759 of ~37k RB3Xenon fns top-match a single rb3-Wii class (BandMachineMgr msg-handler); 90% (6112) are 32-byte/8-insn coverage stubs with sim=1.0

cross_validation_intersection.definition: BinDiff(conf>=0.7) AND BSim(sim>=0.5) agree on same .cpp stem, stub+BandMachineMgr filtered
cross_validation_intersection.note: high per-fn precision but too sparse and non-contiguous to define [start,end) TU spans

root_cause: BSim/BinDiff correctly identify only the distinctive minority of each TU's functions (~2-13%); the trivial accessors and coverage-stub-shaped functions that fill out a TU span are either unmatched or collapse to degenerate generic matches. No contiguous block of correct labels exists to bracket a span. Confirms the roadmap's prior 'coverage-stub mirage + scattered band3 TUs' finding for BSim too.
deliverable_value: crossval_agree.json — 93 unpinned, cross-validated (95%-precision) per-function game-code identity hints. Useful as per-fn LABELS for manual work, NOT as TU-span brackets. Mostly singletons (1-2 fns/stem).
